newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish Polifarbs to invest PLN 200 mln by 2000.
newsitem.headline: Polish Polifarbs to invest PLN 200 mln by 2000.

text.p: Polish paintmakers Polifarb Cieszyn and Polifarb Wroclaw, which seek a mid-year merger, want to invest up to 200 million zlotys by the year 2000, a Wroclaw deputy president said on Monday.

"By the year 2000 we see capital investment of about 200 million zlotys," Wojciech Solarski told a meeting of investors and journalists on the firms' planned merger which is seen by the end of the third quarter this year.

Solarski told Reuters after the meeting that the number represented a preliminary optimistic plan and that as little as 25 million zlotys or 40 million zlotys annually could be invested over the next four years.
Solarski also said that by 2000 the new firm would seek to attain a net operating margin of about one percentage point lower than Wroclaw's 1996 net operating margin of about 10 percent.

Andrzej Jurkiewicz, Polifarb Cieszyn deputy president, said about half the funds from the new entity's planned rights issue to follow the merger would go to boosting production and environmental protection.
He said about a quarter of the funds from the one-for-five rights issue of up to 8.2 million shares would go toward distribution, sales and marketing and investing in other paintmakers.
About 10 percent of the issue, whose record date is due to come after the registration of the new firm, would go toward research and development and 15 percent to working capital. @

Polifarb Cieszyn shareholders will vote on the rights issue of at least four million shares and on the overall merger at their meeting on March 24, as well as on a proposal to name the new entity Polifarb Cieszyn-Wroclaw SA.

The shareholders will vote on a bonus issue of 2,978,820 shares to equal Wroclaw's 22,103,820 shares and set another issue of 22,103,820 shares for Wroclaw shareholders to facilitate a one-for-one share exchange to effect the merger.
Polifarb Cieszyn would take over all the assets of its Wroclaw-based namesake with the new firm based in Wroclaw. @
On March 25 Polifarb Wroclaw's shareholders vote on the merger which would create a firm producing about 40 percent of domestic-made paint and with a 26-percent market share.
